## Background

<!-- Optional. Inline math goes between single dollar signs; a display equation
between double dollar signs. LaTeX syntax:
https://www.overleaf.com/learn/latex/Mathematical_expressions -->

Prediction accuracy is the correlation $r = \mathrm{cor}(\hat{g}, g)$ between
predicted and true breeding values. A common approximation for GBLUP is

$$
r \approx \sqrt{\frac{N h^2}{N h^2 + M_e}}
$$

where $N$ is the training size and $M_e$ the effective number of chromosome
segments.

## Analysis

<!-- One runnable chunk per idea. `#| label:` names the chunk, `#| fig-cap:`
captions the figure. Add `#| echo: false` to hide code entirely, or
`#| eval: false` to show code without running it. Always set a seed. -->

```{python}
#| label: fig-accuracy
#| fig-cap: "Expected genomic prediction accuracy versus training population size"
#| warning: false

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

np.random.seed(42)

M_e = 1000
N = np.arange(100, 5001, 100)
rows = []
for h2 in (0.2, 0.5, 0.8):
    r = np.sqrt(N * h2 / (N * h2 + M_e))
    rows.append(pd.DataFrame({"N": N, "accuracy": r, "h2": f"h² = {h2}"}))
df = pd.concat(rows)

# Plotly figures stay interactive in the rendered post (hover, zoom, legend
# toggling). Swap in matplotlib/seaborn if you prefer a static image.
fig = px.line(df, x="N", y="accuracy", color="h2",
              labels={"N": "Training population size", "accuracy": "Accuracy"},
              template="plotly_white")
fig.show()
```
